Needs changes before merge.

This is a second, independent SAFETY-tier review of the same head. The review comment above (00:16Z) found the `depth_sane` validation problem. This review agrees with it and does not repeat it. This review adds one more blocker: a gouge path.

What looks good:

- `fold_height` measures each reference height along the tool axis. The `+ origin.z` hand-off lands on the local value, as the module doc says.
- Fixed heights and untilted ops keep the old law. The goldens and the 4-axis example do not move.
- The three new tests detect the defect. The decision record and the `Changelog:` line are present. No `CHANGELOG.md` edit. No `crates/ui` change.

Results (locally, in `.claude/worktrees/review-2418`; the PR head already contains upstream main, so the trial merge gave `Already up to date`; no GitHub runner):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| 35 `camcraft-app` test binaries (`tilt_heights`, `tilt`, `tilt_a180`, `tilt_basis_compat`, `opframe_seam`, `opframe_picks`, `heights`, `heights_selection`, `first_4axis_part`, `fourth_axis_pose`, `index_swing`, `index_swing_horizontal`, `rotary_subplate`, `rotary_subplate_standing`, `area_controls`, `area_picks`, `clearance_in_stock`, `top_z_stock_over`, `vertical_rapid_stock`, `self_centering_vise_tilted`, `carried_verify`, `contour_start_point`, `section_mode`, `stock_source_holes`, `setup_align_3d`, `setup_align_hole_kinds`, `fixture_mesh_posed`, `stock_fit_fixtures`, `microarc_test_part`, `post_not_judged`, `machine_switch`, `golden_cl`, `conformance`, `solid_law_goldens`, `tormach_fourth_axis`) | 267 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed |

Mutations (each one reverted after the run):

- `collect_job` without the frame: all three new tests fail (25 vs 15; 17 vs 21; the contour bottom is 13).
- `section_z_of` without the frame: the contour test fails with `no material at z = 14.000`.
- `+ origin.z` removed from `fold_height`: the offset-bar test fails (18 vs 21).

No golden file changes in this PR. `golden_cl`, `conformance` and `solid_law_goldens` pass without changes.

Requested before merge:

1. `crates/app/src/operation/area.rs:172-173` (`whole_model_pocket`) and `crates/app/src/operation/area.rs:220-221` (`stock_pocket`): these functions still read Top and Bottom with `resolve_height` (the setup Z). They use the result for the island ladder planes. The generator levels now come from `fold_height` (along the tool axis). Under a tilt, the two sets of planes are different. The part islands are cut at the wrong planes, and the pocket clears through the part.

   Reproduction (a temporary local test, now removed): stock box 40 x 40 x 50 centred on the origin; part `cube((-10,-5,-15), (10,5,15))`; Pocket, source = the part (or the Stock), tilt A 90 B 0, origin 0; Clearance = Top of stock + 10, Retract = Top of stock + 5, Top = Top of stock + 0, Bottom = Top of model - 2, stepdown 2.

   - With this PR: the levels are at local Z 20 to 3 (correct). But the ladder planes are at the setup Z (25 to 13), so the part sections are empty. The zigzag at local Z 4 and 3 crosses the part, for example move 260: world X -17 to 17 at Y -4, Z -16, with a 6 mm tool. Verification reports 24 `Gouge` warnings and the post is held (48 post-blocking warnings with a part source, 33 with the Stock source).
   - With `collect_job` reverted to the setup resolve (the old behaviour): no warnings.
   - With `fold_height(world, setup, Some(src), frame, top)` and `... bottom)` in the two functions above (a local trial only, removed): all `Gouge` warnings go away.

   The verification law stops the post, so the output is not silent. But the PR changes a clean operation into a path that gouges the part. Use `fold_height` in the two functions. Add a test for a tilted whole-model Pocket (or Adaptive2D / Offset2D) and for a tilted Pocket on the Stock source, with reference heights.

2. The `depth_sane` item in the review above (`crates/app/src/operation/heights_sel.rs:168`).

Notes (not blocking):

- `crates/app/src/operation/material_region.rs:134` and `:163`: the preview places the region at a setup-Z height, but the region is now sectioned along the tool axis. This is display only. Make sure that #2416 includes it.
- `fold_height` reads Top/Bottom of model from `parts_facets_in`. The setup resolve reads `part_aabb_in`. The two sets are different when a model is marked "raw stock only": the tilted read skips that model, the upright read includes it. Please confirm that this is intended.
- `mark_law::budget_of` (`crates/app/src/operation/mark_law.rs:108`) still reads `resolve_params`. A tilted Engrave or Trace that mixes references can get a different mark budget than the path. This is a small risk.
- The PR is a draft and uses `Refs #2389`. This is correct while #2416 is open.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 302b097254569c239d5d5e3f28ff06625080b92c -->

Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.

## What looks good

- A tilted op now measures its reference heights along the tool axis. The new `fold_height` (`crates/app/src/operation/tilt_heights.rs`) returns `z_local + origin.z`, so the existing fold in `run_job` and `source_region` gives the local value. One seam, not two. (`crates/app/src/operation/heights.rs`)
- The upright case is verbatim: A0 B0 and untilted ops read the setup resolve unchanged, so prismatic paths and goldens keep their bits. Fixed heights keep the shipped `h - origin.z` law.
- This obeys the WCS law: no new WCS derivation appears; the WCS shift stays in the `run_job` fold.
- The Prime Directive holds: the null-axis guard is an explicit refusal (`tilt_heights.rs:176` in the diff); no `unwrap()` was added. Degenerate tilt gives a clean error.
- The test file sits in `crates/app/tests/` and imports what `app` defines. Correct placement. The decision record `docs/decisions/2389-tilt-heights-axis.md` matches the code.
- The mutation checks in the body prove the pinning tests can see a regression.
- Body complete: `Changelog:` line, `Fixes #2389`, conventional subject. The display-only planes and the Heights tab echo are split to #2416, correctly.

## Results, merged with main

Trial merge with `origin/main` had no conflicts; the merge commit was local only. Built locally in a review worktree on Windows by this lane's review agent; the diff and law checks were re-read at the endpoints by the maintainer lane.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-app` lib | 223 passed, 0 failed |
| app integration (project round-trip, `tilt`, operations, CLI) | 86 + 12 + 18 passed, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-app --test tilt_heights` (new) | 3 passed, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-ui --lib` | 1055 passed, 0 failed, 6 ignored |
| clippy on the touched crates, `--all-targets -D warnings` | clean, exit 0 |

## Requested before merge

None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

1. A tilted op that uses a Selection reference is refused before the resolver runs. If a future change lets it through, `fold_height` must cover the selection geometry too. Note only.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
